- Tim Hortons: Strong in Canada and growing elsewhere; budget‑friendly drip/iced coffee and donuts; espresso is basic.
- Dunkin’: Common in the US; fast, inexpensive, great for flavored/iced drinks; espresso quality can be hit‑or‑miss.
- Peet’s Coffee: US‑focused; darker, bolder roasts and stronger espresso; fewer locations but good bean quality.
- Caffè Nero: UK/Europe/ME; café ambiance with decent espresso and pastries; quieter than most big chains.
- Pret A Manger: UK/Europe/US; good filter coffee, lots of fresh food; some markets offer attractive coffee subscriptions.
- Dutch Bros: US West; drive‑thru, very friendly, sweet/creative drinks; not ideal for sitting or studying.
- Blue Bottle: US/EU/Asia (limited); high‑quality “third‑wave” espresso and pour‑overs; pricier and fewer locations.
- McCafé: Nearly everywhere; very affordable, basic but consistent.

If you tell me your location and what you value most (espresso quality, sweet drinks, price, quiet workspace, or drive‑thru), I can narrow it to the best pick for you.

Quick picks by scenario
- Enterprise, broad service catalog: AWS. Pros: biggest ecosystem, regions, mature services. Cons: complexity, cost management effort.
- Microsoft-centric orgs: Azure. Pros: AD/Office 365, Windows Server/SQL licensing benefits, good hybrid. Cons: portal quirks, can get pricey.
- Data/AI and Kubernetes: Google Cloud. Pros: BigQuery, Vertex AI, excellent networking, best-in-class GKE. Cons: smaller catalog, fewer enterprise bells/whistles.
- Tight budget/simple infra: Hetzner (best price/perf in EU), OVH, Vultr, DigitalOcean, Linode/Akamai. Pros: predictable, cheap. Cons: fewer managed services, compliance/regions vary.
- Edge/serverless web apps: Cloudflare Workers/Pages with R2/D1, Vercel, Netlify, Fly.io. Pros: global low latency, minimal ops, generous free tiers. Cons: runtime limits, some lock-in, DB choices are narrower.

- Hybrid/regulatory: Azure (Stack/HCI), AWS Outposts, GCP Anthos. Pros: on-prem + cloud consistency. Cons: cost/complexity.

- Commit discounts (1–3 year, savings plans/reservations) can cut 30–60% if workloads are steady.
